morphemes.history: Finland is the land of a thousand lakes; -järvi names them across the interior.
River-mouth and riverside settlements carry -joki throughout the country.
Rapids powered mills and sawmills; -koski marks the old water-power sites.
-lahti dots the lake- and sea-shores where bays gave shelter.
Capes jutting into water are -niemi; classic for shoreline villages.
Dry hilltops above the wet ground became -mäki settlements.
Finland's vast mires gave many places the blunt -suo.
The plain word for village, -kylä, marks old farm clusters.
-vaara, a forested hill, skews to the east and north (Karelian/Savonian land).
Swedish -by hugs the bilingual coast — a second naming tongue along the shore.
Swedish -näs marks coastal capes where Swedish-speakers settled.
Swedish -fors is the coastal twin of inland -koski.
